source_excerpt:
The Volkswagen Tera is expected to be priced between Rs 8 lakh and Rs 13 lakh, ex-showroom. It will become Volkswagen’s most affordable SUV in India, sitting below the Taigun and targeting the high-volume sub-four-metre SUV segment.
The Tera is expected to command a slight premium over the Skoda Kylaq, reflecting its distinct styling, positioning and Volkswagen branding. The final variant-wise pricing will be announced closer to launch.

None of these five is likely before 2027, and Mahindra and Volkswagen are the only ones with even a rough timeline so far.Kia New Sonet: Kia is expected to bring the second-generation Sonet to India in 2027. Like the new Sonet, it will move to the K1 platform, with bigger screens, Level 2 ADAS and more rear-seat room, but there’s no confirmed date yet.Volkswagen Tera is expected around mid-2027, at an estimated Rs 8-13.5 lakh. As a Virtus owner, you’ll find it familiar territory.Mahindra Vision S production version is expected in 2027, and according to our estimates, it will be priced between Rs 10.5-15 lakh.In the case of the Mahindra Vision X, this sporty, crossover-styled SUV was shown as a concept in August 2025 and is expected to go on sale in 2027 and is expected to be under 4m. It will use the new NU_IQ platform, which can take petrol, diesel, hybrid and electric powertrains, but the production engines haven’t been confirmed.In the case of the Hyundai New i20, it made its global debut in Brazil in June, with a more crossover-like look and twin screens. Hyundai hasn’t confirmed an India launch date yet.All of these are estimates, and timelines tend to slip. If you need a car in the next few months, buy from what’s on sale now rather than holding out for any of these.
